name: Arco de Santa Catalina
description: The most iconic landmark of Antigua, this 17th-century arch originally connected a convent to a school, allowing nuns to pass without going out into the street. It is a must-see photo spot with Volcán de Agua in the background.

name: Iglesia de La Merced
address: 6a Avenida Norte y 1a Calle Poniente, Antigua Guatemala
description: A stunning example of Guatemalan ultra-baroque architecture, this church features intricate stucco work on its facade. The monastery ruins and the large fountain are also highlights.

name: Cerro de la Cruz
address: Hilltop on the north side of the city
description: A viewpoint offering panoramic vistas of Antigua and the surrounding volcanoes. The walk up is part of the experience, providing a rewarding view from the cross at the top.

name: Parque Central (Main Square)
description: The heart of the city, this bustling park is surrounded by the Cathedral, government buildings, and numerous shops and restaurants. The central fountain is a popular meeting spot.

name: Convento de las Capuchinas
address: 2a Avenida Norte y 2a Calle Oriente, Antigua Guatemala
description: One of the best-preserved convents in Antigua, it is known for its unique circular tower of cells and beautiful cloisters. It offers a fascinating glimpse into colonial religious life.

name: Casa Santo Domingo
description: A former convent that now serves as a luxury hotel and cultural center. It houses several museums, including colonial art, archaeology, and a pharmacy museum, all set within beautifully restored ruins.

name: Mercado de Artesanías (Artisan Market)
address: Poniente Final, near the main bus terminal
description: A vibrant market where you can find a wide variety of handmade Guatemalan textiles, pottery, woodwork, and jewelry. It's the perfect place to shop for authentic souvenirs.

name: Tanque La Unión
address: 6a Calle Oriente y 2a Avenida Sur, Antigua Guatemala
description: A historic public laundry area (lavadero) with a beautiful fountain, where locals have washed clothes for generations. It is a charming spot that reflects the city's living history.
